IN adds +$1.2M, concentrated in Cirrhosis and Alcoholic Hepatitis with CC.
No admission or paid-per-admit metrics support a clean utilization or unit-cost interpretation because this is a coding or mapping validation pattern.

patterns_data.top_pattern: DC authorized inpatient spend is distorted by facility classification and site-of-care mix
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: DC Medicaid authorized inpatient facility classification and site-of-care mix
patterns_data.pattern_details: DC has a concentrated increase in authorized inpatient spend tied to facility buckets labeled Not Mapped and OTHER. The pattern is present across TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual, with both more admissions and higher paid per admission. This looks like a mix of real site-of-care pressure and facility classification drift, so classification cleanup and business action need to run together.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Without fixing facility attribution, the plan cannot reliably separate true provider mix changes from data classification noise in one of the largest state-level increases.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Correct DC facility mapping for authorized inpatient claims first, then run a focused UM and reimbursement review on the TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual admissions driving the remaining increase.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Facility values of Not Mapped and OTHER mean the plan cannot cleanly determine whether the increase reflects true site-of-care movement, provider mix, or mapping error.
evidence_summary: DC TANF Standard with facility Not Mapped drove +$4.5M from 92 more admissions and about +$31.2K paid per admit.
DC TANF Standard with facility OTHER added +$1.3M with 57 more admissions and about +$1.9K paid per admit.
DC ABD Non Dual with facility Not Mapped added +$0.6M with 16 more admissions and about +$37.7K paid per admit.

This is a concentrated provider economics story, but mapping issues need to be resolved so the true facility and payment picture is clear.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A single-provider concentration of this size can move results quickly, but actions will differ depending on whether the increase is driven by legitimate case severity, facility attribution, or reimbursement terms.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open a joint network, UM, and data-quality review with DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC to separate transplant outliers from mapped inpatient growth and confirm the correct facility attribution on Not Mapped claims.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Not Mapped facility values and a small not-mapped clinical outlier mean provider concentration should be confirmed before taking reimbursement or utilization action.
evidence_summary: DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC heart transplant and assist-system cases added +$1.6M from 3 admissions, including one case at +$1.0M.
DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC TANF Standard Not Mapped utilization added +$1.6M from 20 more admissions despite lower paid per admit, showing volume-led growth.
DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC ABD Non Dual Not Mapped added +$0.8M with 9 more admissions and about +$89.3K paid per admit.
An additional not-mapped DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC clinical case added +$0.2M, reinforcing the attribution issue.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic inpatient cases are creating discrete high-cost spikes
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Rare catastrophic inpatient episodes across UNATTRIBUTED, AR, DC, FL, NC, OH, and VA
key_driver_codes: Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck without Major O.R. Procedures
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Extensive Burns or Full Thickness Burns with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with Skin Graft
ECMO or Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck with Major O.R. Procedures
patterns_data.pattern_details: Several states show isolated catastrophic inpatient episodes rather than a recurring utilization trend. These include tracheostomy and prolonged ventilation, craniotomy, burns, ECMO-level care, transplant, trauma, and other severe cases with very high paid amounts on very small numbers of admissions. The right response is claim-level and clinical validation, not broad policy changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can materially move spend, but they require one-case-at-a-time review instead of broad network or utilization actions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route these cases to clinical and payment integrity review to confirm severity, coding, contract terms, and outlier payment treatment before changing medical policy or provider strategy.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Most of the increase is driven by one-off or very small-count high-cost admissions, so claim-level confirmation is needed before generalizing the pattern.
evidence_summary: A single DC tracheostomy and prolonged mechanical ventilation case added +$1.3M on 1 admission.
A DC craniotomy case added another +$0.7M on 1 admission.
AR trauma, pneumonia, and GI obstruction cases contributed about +$1.0M across 10 admissions.
Rare burn, ECMO, and transplant episodes across FL, NC, OH, and VA added about +$0.9M, led by two SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL cases totaling +$0.6M.

patterns_data.top_pattern: VA spend is concentrated at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL across volume and unit-cost signals
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: VA Medicaid admissions concentrated at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL
patterns_data.pattern_details: VA shows a concentrated provider story at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL. Most of the increase comes from additional admissions in Not Mapped facility claims, while a separate acute-hospital pocket shows unit-cost pressure even as admissions decline. This is a focused provider economics and attribution pattern rather than a broad VA-wide inpatient trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A concentrated provider pattern can often be addressed faster through direct contract, authorization, and data-quality work than through broad market interventions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform a provider-specific review with SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL to fix facility attribution on Not Mapped claims and assess whether the acute-hospital paid-per-admit increase needs reimbursement or UM intervention.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The largest VA drivers sit in Not Mapped facility claims, so facility attribution needs to be corrected to distinguish real provider mix changes from mapping error.
evidence_summary: VA ABD Non Dual Not Mapped volume added +$0.4M at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL.
VA TANF Standard Not Mapped volume added +$0.3M at the same provider.
VA TANF Standard acute hospital added +$0.2M from 21 more admissions even though paid per admit fell slightly.
A separate VA TANF Standard acute-hospital unit-cost increase added +$0.2M while admissions declined by 8, showing reimbursement pressure on top of volume shifts.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Smaller state and product pockets show emerging authorized inpatient pressure
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Smaller Medicaid authorized inpatient pockets across MD, MO, WV, AR, IN, NY, FL, OH, and CO
patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside the largest state and provider concentrations, there is a set of smaller authorized inpatient pockets that are individually modest but together meaningful. These pockets are spread across acute hospital, children's, acute psych, and some Not Mapped facility claims. Most are low-baseline or low-volume, so they should be managed as a targeted exception list rather than as an enterprise trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These pockets are actionable if handled as targeted state-product worklists, but they are too fragmented and low-volume to justify a broad strategy.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Create a state-product exception queue for MD, MO, WV, AR, IN, NY, FL, OH, and CO, and assign each pocket to UM or network teams for targeted review of admission growth, paid-per-admit changes, and any remaining mapping gaps.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Many of these pockets are low-volume, low-baseline, or include Not Mapped facility values, so targeted review should confirm persistence before large-scale action.
evidence_summary: MD, MO, and WV TANF Standard acute hospital added +$1.1M, led by MD bowel procedures at +$0.5M and MO digestive disorders at +$0.5M.
AR LTSS Non Dual added +$0.5M in CHILDRENS and another +$0.3M across Not Mapped and ACUTE PSYCH settings.
IN Family Care acute hospital added +$0.5M across cirrhosis and nerve disorder admissions, and NY Family Care acute hospital added +$0.3M from obesity procedures.
FL, OH, and CO contain smaller ABD or Family Care pockets that are low-volume exceptions rather than a broad trend.
